blocks.text: Private debt consists of loans and debt securities that are not publicly traded, originated or bought by non-bank lenders. It grew strongly after 2008 as banks retreated from middle-market lending under tighter regulation.
Direct lending

items: Loans made directly to (usually sponsor-backed) **middle-market** companies, mostly **senior secured** and **floating rate** (reference rate + spread).
**Unitranche**: a single loan combining senior and junior debt at a blended rate, simplifying the capital structure.
Returns come from the spread, upfront fees (OID) and an **illiquidity premium**; floating rates limit interest-rate risk.

**Covenants**: maintenance covenants (tested regularly, e.g., leverage ≤ 5x) give lenders early warning; incurrence covenants apply only when the borrower takes an action. **Covenant-lite** loans have few or no maintenance covenants.

blocks.text: Mezzanine debt

items: Subordinated debt ranking below senior loans but above equity, often unsecured.
Return from cash coupon + **PIK** (payment-in-kind) interest + **equity kickers** (warrants, conversion rights).
Used in LBOs and growth financings to fill the gap between senior debt and equity.

blocks.text: Distressed debt

items: Buying debt of companies in or near default at deep discounts (e.g., yields > 1,000 bp over Treasuries).
**Fulcrum security**: the most senior class that is not fully covered by the firm’s value — it will likely be converted into the reorganized company’s equity, giving control (**loan-to-own**).

**Chapter 11** (US): reorganization under court protection; the firm continues operating. **Chapter 7**: liquidation. **Prepackaged** bankruptcy: plan negotiated with creditors before filing → faster and cheaper.
**Absolute priority rule**: senior claims are paid in full before junior claims receive anything (deviations happen in practice).
**DIP financing** (debtor-in-possession): new money lent during Chapter 11 with super-priority status.
Strategies can be **active** (seeking influence or control) or **passive** (trading on mispricing).

blocks.text: Other segments
Venture debt, asset-based lending, specialty finance (royalties, receivables, litigation finance), real estate and infrastructure debt.

La **fulcrum security** est la tranche de dette « pivot » : celle qui sera convertie en actions lors de la restructuration. Le **DIP financing** est remboursé en priorité parce qu’il permet à l’entreprise de continuer à fonctionner.

fiches.title: Credit Risk and Credit Models
fiches.fr: Le risque de crédit et ses modèles

blocks.label: Expected loss
blocks.tex: EL = PD \times LGD \times EAD, \qquad LGD = 1 - RR

blocks.text: Observed spreads are usually **larger** than expected losses alone because they also include risk premia for default uncertainty, illiquidity and taxes.
Structural models (Merton)

items: Default occurs when the value of the firm’s **assets** falls below the face value of its **debt** at maturity.
**Equity** = a **call option** on the firm’s assets with strike = face value of debt.
**Risky debt** = risk-free debt − a **put option** on the firm’s assets (the lenders are short a put).
Higher asset volatility → higher equity value and **lower** debt value (wider spreads).

blocks.tex: E = \text{Call}(V, F), \qquad D = F e^{-rT} - \text{Put}(V, F)

blocks.text: Reduced-form models
Default is modeled as a random event driven by a **hazard rate** (default intensity $\lambda$), calibrated to market prices (spreads, CDS) rather than to the firm’s balance sheet.
Seniority and recovery
Recovery rates decline with seniority: senior secured loans recover the most, then senior unsecured bonds, subordinated debt, and equity (usually little or nothing).
Credit default swaps
The **protection buyer** pays a periodic premium (the CDS spread) and receives compensation (par − recovery) if a credit event occurs; the **protection seller** is long credit risk.
Merton : l’action est un **call** sur les actifs ; le prêteur a **vendu un put**. Plus les actifs sont volatils, plus l’action vaut cher et plus la dette perd de la valeur.

A **collateralized loan obligation (CLO)** is an actively managed special-purpose vehicle that buys a diversified pool of **leveraged loans** and finances it by issuing tranches of debt (AAA down to BB/B) and an **equity** tranche.

items: **Waterfall**: interest and principal are paid sequentially from the senior tranches down to equity; losses hit equity first.
**Coverage tests**: overcollateralization (OC) and interest coverage (IC) tests. If a test fails, cash flows are **diverted** from junior tranches and equity to pay down senior notes.
**Reinvestment period** (often several years) during which the manager reinvests principal; then the CLO amortizes.
**Equity tranche**: receives the residual excess spread — a leveraged exposure (≈ 8–12x) to loan spreads and defaults.
The CLO “arbitrage” is the difference between the yield on the loans and the cost of the liabilities.

blocks.text: Senior CLO tranches have historically shown very low default rates; the risk is concentrated in junior tranches and equity.
Tranching does not remove risk from the pool; it **redistributes** it. Correlation of defaults matters: higher correlation hurts senior tranches (more extreme outcomes) and can benefit equity.
Si les tests OC/IC échouent, la **trésorerie est détournée** vers le remboursement des tranches seniors : la tranche equity ne reçoit plus rien tant que le test n’est pas rétabli.

formulas.name: Expected loss
formulas.tex: EL = PD \times LGD \times EAD, \quad LGD = 1 - RR

formulas.name: Credit spread approximation
formulas.vars: $\lambda$ intensité de défaut, $RR$ taux de recouvrement.

formulas.name: Merton model

formulas.name: Survival probability (constant hazard rate)
formulas.tex: P(\text{no default by } T) = e^{-\lambda T}

questions.q: Direct lending loans to middle-market companies are typically:
questions.explain: Le direct lending est majoritairement **senior sécurisé** et à **taux variable** (référence + spread).

questions.q: Why does a floating-rate direct lending portfolio carry relatively little interest-rate (duration) risk?
options: Coupons reset with the reference rate, so prices are less sensitive to rate changes
The loans are always hedged with swaps
questions.explain: Les coupons se **réajustent** avec le taux de référence : la duration est très courte. Le risque principal est le **crédit**.

questions.q: A unitranche facility:
options: Combines senior and junior debt into a single loan with one blended rate
Is a loan split into many tranches sold to the public
Is always subordinated to mezzanine debt
questions.explain: **Unitranche** = une seule ligne qui remplace dette senior + dette junior, à un taux mixte.

questions.q: The main disadvantage of covenant-lite loans for lenders is that:
options: They provide less early warning and fewer opportunities to intervene before default
They prohibit the borrower from refinancing
questions.explain: Sans **covenants de maintien**, le prêteur ne peut pas intervenir tôt quand la situation se dégrade ; les recouvrements peuvent être plus faibles.

questions.q: A covenant that is tested only when the borrower takes a specific action, such as issuing new debt, is a(n):
questions.explain: Le covenant **d’incurrence** n’est vérifié qu’au moment d’une action (nouvelle dette, dividende, acquisition).

questions.q: Mezzanine debt typically ranks:
options: Below senior debt but above equity
questions.explain: La **mezzanine** est subordonnée à la dette senior mais passe avant les actionnaires.

questions.q: Which return component is most characteristic of mezzanine financing compared with senior loans?
options: Equity kickers such as warrants, plus PIK interest
questions.explain: La mezzanine compense sa subordination par des intérêts **PIK** et des **equity kickers** (bons de souscription).

questions.q: In a restructuring, the “fulcrum security” is:
options: The most senior class of claims that is not fully covered by the firm’s value
questions.explain: La **fulcrum security** est la tranche où la valeur s’épuise : elle sera en général convertie en actions de l’entreprise restructurée.

questions.q: A bankrupt firm is worth USD 500 million. It has USD 300 million of senior secured debt, USD 400 million of senior unsecured bonds and USD 200 million of subordinated debt. Under absolute priority, which class is the fulcrum security?
questions.explain: Senior sécurisé : 300 remboursés intégralement. Il reste 200 pour 400 de senior unsecured (50 % de recouvrement) → ce sont les **senior unsecured** qui deviennent propriétaires. Le subordonné et les actions ne reçoivent rien.

questions.q: Under US law, a Chapter 11 filing generally leads to:
options: Reorganization of the firm while it continues operating
Automatic repayment of all creditors in full
Conversion of the firm into a public entity
questions.explain: **Chapter 11** = réorganisation sous protection du tribunal ; **Chapter 7** = liquidation.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a prepackaged bankruptcy?
options: It shortens the process and reduces costs because creditors approved the plan before filing
It eliminates the absolute priority rule
It guarantees full recovery to equity holders
questions.explain: Le plan étant **négocié avant le dépôt**, la procédure est plus rapide et moins coûteuse (moins de destruction de valeur).

questions.q: Debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing is attractive to lenders mainly because:
options: It receives super-priority status over existing claims
It is guaranteed by the government
questions.explain: Le **DIP** bénéficie d’une **super-priorité** accordée par le tribunal : risque faible pour un rendement souvent attractif.

questions.q: A hedge fund buys the fulcrum bonds of a distressed company intending to become its controlling shareholder after restructuring. This strategy is called:
questions.explain: **Loan-to-own** : acheter la dette pivot pour en obtenir le contrôle via la conversion en actions.

questions.q: A loan of USD 20 million has a 3% probability of default and a 40% recovery rate. Its expected loss is:
questions.explain: $EL = 3\% \times (1 - 40\%) \times 20\text{M} = 0{,}03 \times 0{,}6 \times 20\text{M} = 360\,000$ USD.

questions.q: A bond’s default intensity is 2.5% per year and its expected recovery rate is 40%. Its approximate credit spread is:
Observed credit spreads are generally larger than the expected loss rate because they also include:
options: Risk premia for default uncertainty and illiquidity
The equity risk premium of the lender
questions.explain: Le spread rémunère la perte attendue **plus** des primes de risque (incertitude des défauts, illiquidité, fiscalité).

questions.q: In the Merton model, the equity of a levered firm is equivalent to:
options: A call option on the firm’s assets with a strike equal to the face value of debt
A put option on the firm’s assets
A short call on the firm’s debt
questions.explain: Les actionnaires reçoivent max(V − F, 0) à l’échéance : c’est un **call** sur les actifs de strike F.

questions.q: According to the Merton model, an increase in the volatility of a firm’s assets, all else equal, will:
options: Increase equity value and decrease the value of risky debt
Decrease both equity and debt values
Increase debt value and decrease equity value
questions.explain: La volatilité augmente la valeur du **call** (actions) et du **put** vendu par les prêteurs : la dette perd de la valeur, les spreads s’élargissent.

questions.q: Reduced-form credit models differ from structural models in that they:
options: Model default as a random event with an intensity calibrated to market prices
Require the firm’s asset value and volatility
Assume default only at debt maturity
Treat equity as a call option
questions.explain: Les modèles **à forme réduite** modélisent le défaut par une **intensité (hazard rate)** calibrée sur les spreads, sans modéliser le bilan.

questions.q: Which class of claims typically has the highest recovery rate in default?
questions.explain: Les **prêts seniors sécurisés** récupèrent le plus (garanties + rang). Les recouvrements baissent avec la subordination.

questions.q: Compared with high-yield bonds, leveraged loans typically:
options: Pay floating rates and are secured, with higher recoveries
Pay fixed rates and offer call protection
questions.explain: Les **leveraged loans** : taux variable, sûretés, rang senior, remboursables au pair. Les obligations high yield : taux fixe, souvent non sécurisées, protection contre le remboursement anticipé.

questions.q: In a credit default swap, the protection seller:
options: Receives periodic premiums and pays par minus recovery if a credit event occurs
Pays periodic premiums and receives par if a credit event occurs
questions.explain: Le **vendeur de protection** encaisse la prime et paie (pair − recouvrement) en cas d’événement de crédit : il est **long risque de crédit**.

questions.q: The collateral of a typical CLO consists mainly of:
questions.explain: Un **CLO** détient un portefeuille diversifié de **leveraged loans** seniors sécurisés.

questions.q: If a CLO fails its overcollateralization test:
options: Cash flows are diverted from junior tranches and equity to pay down senior notes
The equity tranche receives a bonus payment
questions.explain: L’échec d’un test **OC** détourne la trésorerie vers le remboursement des tranches seniors jusqu’au rétablissement du ratio.

questions.q: The equity tranche of a CLO is best described as:
options: A leveraged exposure to the excess spread of the loan pool that absorbs losses first
A fixed-rate claim with no default exposure
A tranche paid before the senior notes
questions.explain: La tranche **equity** touche le résiduel (excess spread) avec un fort effet de levier, et subit les pertes en premier.

questions.q: In a tranched credit structure, an increase in default correlation among the underlying loans, holding expected losses constant, tends to:
options: Hurt senior tranches and benefit the equity tranche
Benefit senior tranches and hurt the equity tranche
Have no effect on any tranche
questions.explain: Une corrélation plus forte rend les scénarios extrêmes plus probables : plus de chances que les pertes atteignent les **seniors**, mais aussi plus de scénarios sans pertes pour l’**equity**.

questions.q: Which factor contributed most to the growth of private direct lending after 2008?
options: Banks reduced middle-market lending under stricter regulation
Interest rates on loans were capped by law
questions.explain: Après 2008, la **régulation bancaire** (capital, Bâle III) a réduit les prêts des banques aux PME/ETI, laissant la place aux prêteurs non bancaires.

questions.q: With a constant default intensity of 4% per year, the probability that a borrower survives 5 years without defaulting is closest to:
